scope: Independent offline PDB MSF/TPI/public-symbol decoding, fixed original PE disassembly and installed SDK inspection only. No native target execution, VM access, debugger connection, new parser tool or frozen-source modification.
decision: Raw KD CONTEXT plus PRCB special-register blocks do not constitute unmodified complete57 state. Read bounded raw blocks only as explicitly qualified development evidence; do not manufacture missing fields.
pdb_method: Read retained MSF streams directly with Python struct; resolve complete LF_STRUCTURE/LF_FIELDLIST/LF_MEMBER records including numeric leaves and CodeView padding, and S_PUB32 section-relative addresses. Multiple KPRCB/KPCR definitions retained; full definitions and smaller prefix definitions agree on the used offsets. No DbgHelp execution or PDB download.

IDebugAdvanced_GetThreadContext.format: Target effective processor CONTEXT, not automatically WOW64_CONTEXT. Confirm IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64=0x8664 and actual stopped processor/thread; do not switch to x86 effective mode and reinterpret returned bytes.
IDebugAdvanced_GetThreadContext.flags: Preserve returned ContextFlags at +0x30 and every raw byte. AMD64 group bits: CONTROL1, INTEGER2, SEGMENTS4, FLOAT8, DEBUG0x10, XSTATE0x40 with architecture0x100000. Group flag is necessary but not sufficient for architectural provenance on this kernel path. GetThreadContext is an output API, not a hardware FXSAVE request.
IDebugAdvanced_GetThreadContext.extended: Base0x4d0 does not contain arbitrary extended-state payload; refuse claiming XSTATE coverage without validated buffer format, offset/length, masks and supported component layout.

api_contract.PRCB_location: ReadProcessorSystemData(current CPU, DEBUG_DATA_KPRCB_OFFSET=1) can return an 8-byte PRCB address. CLI alternative: poi(@+0x20), crosschecked against current CPU/thread.
api_contract.stale_embedded_context: PDB ProcessorState starts at PRCB+0x100 and ContextFrame at +0xf0 within it, hence PRCB+0x1f0. Actual current save/report/get paths use pointer at PRCB+0x8980 and flags at +0x8988. Never substitute embedded ContextFrame by name alone.

kernel_provenance_findings.claim: General CONTROL/INTEGER fields are reconstructed from the debug exception trap/exception frames, not from the original syscall user frame. At this stop RIP is the 64-bit kernel tail, and live RAX is the wait result.
KeContextFromKframes writes DS=ES=0x2b and FS=0x53, GS=0x2b as constants when SEGMENTS is requested. These are normalized context values, not captured segment selectors.

Its FLOAT path tests trap SegCs bit0; for kernel-origin CS0x10 the FXSAVE at 0x2a71d5 is skipped. It still copies XMM0..5 from debug trap and XMM6..15 from debug exception frame, and MXCSR from trap. Thus FltSave x87 header/register bytes cannot be certified from FLOAT flag or nonzero data alone.

KiDispatchException creates a local context; kernel-mode path skips its user-mode zeroing branch and later calls KeContextFromKframes. The KD report path copies 0x4d0 bytes from that context into PRCB.Context before reporting. Unpopulated x87 bytes are not repaired by the copy.

Separate KiSaveProcessorState has a conditional FXSAVE helper before frame conversion, but this does not establish that the context exposed for the current kernel #DB retains those bytes after the later report-copy. Do not conflate other-CPU freeze save with current fault-context provenance.

SpecialRegisters captures CR0/2/3/4 and debug registers on debugger entry. It writes LDTR=0 instead of SLDT; two globals can bypass SGDT/SIDT/STR. Its MsrGsBase/MsrFsBase/etc structure members are not refreshed by this routine.

The save routine clears hardware DR7 after saving it. Kernel ba changes debug-register usage and #DB changes debug status; these observed registers are not the untouched application debug state. CONTEXT debug fields may additionally be normalized to zero when trap DR7 mask0x355 is clear.

prerequisites: actual kernel/wow64cpu/x86 ntdll file identities and runtime bases
one stopped epoch; actual event CPU/thread/process and RIP=kernel+0x6fcc6a
do not issue .cxr/.trap/.thread/.effmach switching before raw stop capture
reject unreadable/short blocks, invalid pointers or identity disagreement; no fallback zero

definitions.P: current PRCB from independently crosschecked PCR/current CPU
definitions.C: poi(P+0x8980); validate alignment, current flags and matching raw RIP/RSP/thread epoch before use
definitions.U: original syscall trap base = captured kernel RBP-0x80; must match caller/path
definitions.B: native user R13 preserved as nonvolatile by this syscall path; authenticate WOW64 TLS relation before treating R13-0x80 as CPU reserved area

optional_small_bridge_reads: qword at original native user RSP=poi(U+0x180) must identify wow64cpu+0x1b56 after ret from +0x1cf3
dword [B+0x3c] expected x86 ntdll NtWait+0xc; dword [B+0x48] original x86 return stack
actual original x86 caller word at [B+0x48] plus 12 argument bytes; first three kernel returns also need timeout/handle identity
GDT entry bytes referenced by actual selectors/TR require validated 64-bit GDTR Base+limit; descriptor memory does not automatically equal cached hidden descriptor state

canonical57_groups.fields: EAX EBX ECX EDX ESI EDI EBP ESP EIP EFLAGS
canonical57_groups.availability: AMD64 CONTEXT has 64-bit GPR/RIP plus EFlags; preserve full width. Kernel RSP/RBP/RIP and volatile values are already kernel-state values. Do not truncate them into x86 canonical57. Candidate user GPRs require original trap and WOW64 return semantics.

canonical57_groups.fields: FPCW FPSW FPTAG FIP FDP FCS FDS FOP FP0 FP1 FP2 FP3 FP4 FP5 FP6 FP7
canonical57_groups.availability: No certified current kernel #DB x87 source in the reviewed context-copy path. Legacy FXSAVE storage format alone is not validity. Existing KTHREAD.StateSaveArea/XStateSave pointers may be stale, nested or thread-save data; ownership/currentness needs separate proof.

canonical57_groups.fields: MXCSR XMM0 XMM1 XMM2 XMM3 XMM4 XMM5 XMM6 XMM7
canonical57_groups.availability: Debug trap/exception-frame reconstruction is a bounded source for interrupted kernel SIMD with matching flags/path; original syscall user trap saves are conditional. Common exit loads trap MXCSR and zeros XMM0..5, so kernel-tail SIMD is not the eventual user postreturn set.

canonical57_groups.fields: CS DS ES FS GS SS
canonical57_groups.availability: CS/SS derive from debug trap; DS/ES/FS/GS are normalized constants in context conversion. Hidden bases/limits/access and 64-bit GS swap state are absent. Original user CS/SS come from original syscall trap, later WOW64 transition produces CS0x23/SS0x2b.

SpecialRegisters stores 64-bit values on debugger entry, later than breakpoint exception arrival. CR3 can change on shadow return; CR2 may be affected by intervening fault handling. Not inherently pre-call/user-return controls.

GDTR/IDTR have 16-bit limits and 64-bit bases at Special+0x56/+0x58 and +0x66/+0x68 when SGDT/SIDT branch ran. TR selector at +0x70; LDTR +0x72 is synthesized zero. Descriptor hidden caches not captured. Do not equate null-looking fields or current GDT bytes with complete cached state.

canonical57_groups.fields: DR0 DR1 DR2 DR3 DR4 DR5 DR6 DR7
canonical57_groups.availability: Only DR0..3/6/7 have context/special slots. DR4/5 are not independent readable storage: CR4.DE controls alias-to-DR6/7 versus #UD. Do not add arbitrary zero slots. Applied ba/#DB affects DR contents; app-pristine debug state and simulator-specific DR4/5 contract are not recovered.

fx_format_rules.source_format_gate: Only parse a demonstrably valid FXSAVE image. Reviewed opcodes 0f ae /0 have no REX.W: FIP/FDP are 32-bit offset fields plus selectors, not 64-bit pointers. High pointer halves cannot be fabricated. CPUID.7.0 EBX13/6 semantics require actual guest CPUID evidence before accepting architectural-zero/pointer-update behavior.
fx_format_rules.offsets_relative_to_valid_FXSAVE: FCW0:2, FSW2:2, abridged FTW4:1, FOP6:2, FIP8:4/FCS12:2, FDP16:4/FDS20:2, MXCSR24:4, ST slots32+16*i (10 meaningful bytes), XMM160+16*i
fx_format_rules.canonical_mapping: canonical FPn are physical. TOP=(FSW>>11)&7; physical n uses logical slot (n-TOP)&7. FTW bits are physical; do not rotate FTW. Full tags: empty3; exponent0/mantissa0 zero1; exponent0 or0x7fff or integer-bit-clear special2; otherwise valid0. Preserve raw empty slot payload rather than inventing bytes.
fx_format_rules.scope: These rules do not cure missing/unrefreshed x87 state in the kernel #DB context.

original_flow: Kernel tail +0x6fcc6a add rsp,0x38; ret to verified dispatcher normally +0x428c35.

Kernel return includes pending APC/instrumentation/debug/shadow/CET branches. Common path loads MXCSR at +0x428d86, changes DRs conditionally, zeros XMM0..5 and RDX, loads user RIP/RFLAGS and RSP/RBP, swapgs/sysretq; do not assume all other paths inactive.
Native user saved RIP must equal loaded wow64cpu base+0x1cf3 for syscall branch; int2e alternative is +0x1cf6. Ret pops native user stack to +0x1b56.
wow64cpu +0x1b56/+1b5a/+1b5e/+1b62 restore EDI/ESI/EBX/EBP from [R13+0x20/24/28/38]. +1b66 tests-and-clears flag bit0 at [R13-0x80].

Flag0 clear: +1b6e..1b8e builds far pointer with CS0x23 and [R13+0x3c], loads SS0x2b and ESP=[R13+0x48], then far-jumps. Flag set: +1b91..1bc4 builds an IRET frame using saved EFLAGS at +0x44, stack at+0x48 and RIP at+0x3c, then iretq.

Expected x86 return is ntdll runtime base+0x73bfc: original instruction c2 0c 00 (ret12). It pops x86 caller address and consumes 12 argument bytes. Confirm actual native user stack/R13 memory/runtime relocation before linking it to fixture/game postcall.
wow64_bridge.cpu_reserved_layout_inference: Original +0x1660/1670/1678 sets R13=poi(TEB64+0x1488)+0x80. SDK WOW64_CONTEXT field alignment matches Context=R13-0x7c; reserved area starts R13-0x80. ExtendedRegisters begins R13+0x50 and XMM0 R13+0xf0. This layout match does not prove freshness: fast entry +0x1779..17ab writes selected GP/flags only, not complete x87/FX state.
wow64_bridge.no_direct_fx_restore_on_selected_return: The selector13 return block +0x1b56..1bc4 contains no FXSAVE/FXRSTOR and no XMM reload. Other WOW64 entry/slow paths differ; do not import their behavior into this path.
wow64_bridge.original_ntdll_export: PE export NtWaitForSingleObject RVA0x73bf0, selector eax0x000d0004; call edx; ret12 at+0xc. Trampoline RVA0x96710 jumps through Wow64Transition RVA0x12b220. Relocated immediate differs from on-disk preferred base and must be checked as relocation, not a patch.
unresolved: No complete dynamic branch trace from kernel epilogue through SYSRET/IRET/shadow exit, WOW64 far transition and x86 RET has been captured by this static review.
Pending APC/instrumentation may change the intended user context after this tail. A snapshot here is not a deterministic full interval unless those paths and memory inputs are accounted for.
x87/current user extended-state ownership, hidden segment caches, authoritative LDTR and pristine debug state remain missing.
Even successful own-fixture stops would not establish original-game handshake, resource lifetime or canonical57 acceptance.
